catalog_quote: 2.1 Overview of basic features. The common basic elements of the phonology of Seko languages are stated in the following list. ... 7. Stress is penultimate. 8. Closed syllables are common. Closed syllable structure is maintained when adding stress-shifting suffixes. ... 10. Possessive suffixes, which all begin with consonants and are stress-shifting, only attach to stem-final codas. ... 2.2 More about prosodic features ... VOWEL LENGTH occurs in word final position, where it is contrastive. Length can occur on any of the five vowels. Word stress does not shift, but remains penultimate. Consider the following two-syllable roots from Seko Padang. (1) a. mata ‘eye’ a'. mata: ‘raw’ ... VOWEL QUICKNESS is contrastive only in the stressed syllable (penultimate position). ... Normally, a penultimate closed syllable nucleus is followed by two consonants, like the /a/ is followed by /nd/ in example (6) from Seko Tengah. ... (6) tanduk ‘horn’
world_status: statement found in a copy we already had

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (56 pp, born-digital text layer, pdftk 2006; byte-identical size 407249 to the live open copy at https://sil-philippines-languages.org/ical/papers/laskowske-Proto%20Seko.pdf, HTTP 200 today). extracted text of pp.1-5: title page names the four languages 'Seko Padang, Seko Tengah, Panasuan, and Budong-budong.. based on several years of fieldwork in this area'; sec. 2 'Seko Synchronic Phonology', 2.1 'Overview of basic features' -- 'The common basic elements of the phonology of Seko languages are stated in the following list.' p.3 item 7 'Stress is penultimate.'; item 8 'Closed syllables are common. Closed syllable structure is maintained when adding stress-shifting suffixes.';…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In all four Seko languages, Seko Tengah included, word stress falls on the penultimate syllable; consonant-initial possessive suffixes shift stress rightward to keep it penultimate; a contrastive word-final long vowel does not attract or move stress (stress stays on the syllable before it); the vowel-quickness contrast is licensed only in the stressed penult.
new_statements.exceptions: Word-final long vowels (mata: 'raw' etc.) do not shift stress; the Seko Padang echo vowel -i is described as non-stress-shifting (Seko Padang only). Seko Tengah-specific: prefix vowels lowered (mu-/mi- > mo-/me-) in pre-penultimate, i.e. unstressed, position. No lexical exceptions listed for Seko Tengah.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a synchronic overview prefacing a comparative reconstruction; explicitly scoped as common to Seko Padang, Seko Tengah, Panasuan and Budong-budong, based on the author's own fieldwork (several years in the Seko area); examples are citation forms, one of them (tanduk) from Seko Tengah. Not a Seko Tengah-specific description.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is scoped over the whole Seko group (Seko Padang seko1243, Seko Tengah seko1242, Panasuan pana1305, Budong-budong budo1241) by a fieldworker who worked in the area; it is not a Seko Tengah-only description, but Seko Tengah is explicitly named as one of the four languages covered and supplies one of the illustrating forms (tanduk). The same file is already the the deciding source for seko1243 and budo1241 in this reading. Grimes & Grimes 1987's SEK wordlist (one Seko Tengah speaker) is consistent: default penultimate, apostrophes only where a final double vocoid makes the count ambiguous.

sources.note: Seko Family entry pp.52-53 (Seko Tengah = Pewanean): classification only. Wordlist 'Symbols' p.94: 'Stress in South Sulawesi languages usually occurs on the penultimate syllable. In such cases it is not marked in the word lists. Where stress deviates.. or where stress may be unclear due to double vocoids, etc., it is marked with an apostrophe'. The single SEK (Seko Tengah) wordlist carries apostrophes mostly before syllables followed by a final double vocoid ('reaa 'blood', 'kitaa, ki'nandee, 'koii, 'suaa, 'inaa), i.e. root-penultimate stress plus final long vowel, consistent with Laskowske.
